public_inputs.task:
# Coalesce draft saves in the workspace

The editor currently writes to the workspace store on every edit. Change editor
autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save
only its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate.
Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior. Keep
search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task.

limitations: Departure flushing is a preservation strategy derived from existing immediate persistence and TASK, not an explicit universal before-return deadline.
Only attempt 1 is supplied. Its acceptance verdict and syntax check passed; no supplied behavioral observations establish causality or cross-task benefit.
Public documentation establishes navigation from saved integrations, not reentry from output sinks, scheduler operations or subscription cleanup. Exception recovery is unspecified.
The supplied Ruby sources do not establish Vue unmount integration or admitted decoding and audit obligations.

rules.body: Apply when per-document pending work survives presentation retirement and saving can synchronously navigate. README.md states: "Document body, per-document buffer and navigation outline are separate responsibilities." It also states: "Workspace coordinates visits; saved integrations may synchronously navigate and outline retains a breadcrumb archive." src/workflow.rb provides reusable buffers through "def get(env,id);@entries[id] ||= Trailing.new(env,120) {|text| env.write(id,text)};end".

Capture the current view and enqueue an acceptance-time copy of its text in that view's document buffer. Preserve the no-current-view no-op and original document association. TASK states: "autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save\nonly its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate." Existing src/workflow.rb immediately copies stored text with "@records[id] = text.dup.freeze"; deferring that copy until consumption would allow caller mutation to change accepted text. Keep separate reusable buffers rather than redirecting pending text through the later current view.

Retire consumed pending state before invoking callback-capable work so nested flushing cannot duplicate it and nested edits can establish another burst. Preserve src/workflow.rb ordering: "value = @pending\n    @handle = @pending = nil\n    @work.call(value) unless value.nil?". Empty text must remain consumable.

Capture the departing view, revoke its current ownership, detach its captured subscription and finish its clearing presentation before flushing its buffer. Preserve the reusable buffer. TASK states: "Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior." The original src/workflow.rb edit path is "def edit(text);view=@current;@env.write(view.id,text) if view;end". Flushing pending text during departure preserves synchronous store availability across switch, same-document reopen, close and dispose while permitting active editing to coalesce. Ownership alone does not establish this scheduling requirement for other tasks.

Guard both editor installation and workspace projection publication against navigation invoked during saving. Recheck the editor request generation after retirement, and recheck the workspace epoch after editor open or close before committing or clearing the projection. src/workflow.rb already captures "@generation+=1;request=@generation" and "@epoch+=1;mine=@epoch". docs/host-api.md states: "Store reads values and synchronously notifies saved integrations." Nested navigation must retain its selection, document rendering, visit identity and projection; an outer stale clear is also an unauthorized visible effect.

Preserve current-document status filtering, captured subscription cleanup, store event identity/text/revision semantics and copied breadcrumb history. src/workflow.rb filters with "if e[:id]==id", detaches with "def detach;@env.store.stop(@token);end", and publishes trail copies with "@trail.map(&:dup)". docs/host-api.md states: "Document and projection sinks carry visit identifiers; committed outline keeps a copied breadcrumb trail." Clearing selection must retain the existing breadcrumb archive.

Keep transient preview policy separate from durable document edits. TASK states: "Keep\nsearch preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task." Preserve src/workflow.rb: "def initialize(env);@task=Trailing.new(env,40){|q| env.output('preview',{'query'=>q})};end" and "def hide;@task.cancel;end". Do not infer audit or decoding retention requirements from breadcrumb preservation.

Verify latest-only saving after 120 ms of quiet, later independent bursts, empty text, mutation of caller-owned text after acceptance and editing with no current view. Exercise pending edits across switch, same-document reopen, close and dispose; check original-document persistence, buffer reuse and captured subscription removal. Trigger nested select and close from timer-driven and departure-driven saves; check final selection, document/projection visit agreement, breadcrumb copies, successor rendering and subsequent nested edits. Confirm preview retains its 40 ms delay and hide cancellation. These checks operationalize TASK's coalescing and preservation instructions; they are not claims about supplied behavioral test coverage.

checkpoints: Several edits within 120 ms produce one save containing the latest accepted text; later bursts save independently, including empty text.
Switch, same-document reopen, close, and dispose with pending text preserve that text on its original document and make it available before the departure operation returns.
A saved integration that synchronously selects or closes during departure leaves its resulting selection, document rendering, and projection authoritative.
Timer-driven saves that trigger navigation do not leave retired subscriptions active or disrupt subsequent edits.
Projection publications retain copied breadcrumb history, and preview retains its existing delay and cancellation behavior.
forbidden_effects: Saving every edit immediately instead of coalescing active editing bursts.
Dropping accepted pending text on retirement or saving it under a successor document's identity.
Allowing an outer navigation operation to overwrite selection or projection established by nested navigation during a save.
Clearing a successor's document rendering after a callback has installed it.
Canceling durable document edits as though they were transient preview work.
Changing tests, configuration, or search preview behavior.
lifecycle_identity: A visit identifies a document presentation; reopening the same document creates a distinct visit.
BufferBank retains a separate reusable trailing task per document across view retirement.
Each accepted edit belongs to the document and buffer current when edit is called.
Badge owns its captured store subscription; retirement must detach that subscription without affecting a successor's resources.
Editor generation and Workspace epoch distinguish an outer navigation request from navigation invoked synchronously during its callbacks.

obligations.text: Route edits accepted by the current editor through its document buffer, saving only the latest text after a 120 ms quiet interval. Preserve subsequent bursts and the existing no-current-editor no-op.
Preserve accepted text and its original document identity across deferred saving, including the existing copy semantics of stored text.

Flush the captured departing document's pending edits during switch, reopen, close, and dispose so persistence remains available synchronously when these operations return. Retain the reusable document buffer.
Retire consumed pending state before invoking the callback-capable save, allowing reentrant edits to establish independent pending work and preventing duplicate consumption.

Make retirement and navigation safe when saved integrations synchronously navigate: clean up the departing subscription and presentation, and prevent superseded outer operations from installing a document, committing a projection, or clearing a successor.
Preserve document and projection visit identifiers, current-document status filtering, store event payload semantics, and copied breadcrumb history.
Keep search preview's 40 ms trailing publication and hide cancellation unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Capture the current view and its persistent buffer when accepting an edit; later navigation must not redirect that work.
Trailing.flush must clear its handle and pending value before invoking work, as the existing utility already does.

Revoke the departing view's ownership and complete its subscription cleanup and clearing presentation before callback-capable flushing, or otherwise guard any remaining visible effects against successor ownership.
After departure flushing returns, Editor.open must recheck its request generation before installing a view.
After editor navigation returns, Workspace must recheck its navigation epoch before committing or clearing the projection.
preservation: Existing departure operations leave accepted edits persisted before returning; introducing autosave delay must not weaken that observable navigation behavior.
Store notifications remain synchronous, with original id, text, and revision semantics.
Document buffers remain independent and reusable across visits.
Valid navigation continues to publish matching document and projection visit identifiers.
Projection.clear preserves the breadcrumb archive, and published trails remain copies.
Status events remain filtered by document identity, and retired subscriptions are removed.
Search preview timing, payload, and cancellation remain unchanged.

rules.body: Apply when delayed edits belong to a persistent document owner while the current view owns a subscription, and saving can synchronously navigate. docs/host-api.md states: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription." It also states: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously."

Capture the current document buffer when accepting an edit and enqueue its text there. Retain the original document identity and persistent buffer reuse across view retirement. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/coordinator.js already binds each buffer's consumer with "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))".

Before a callback-capable save, snapshot and retire the consumed pending state so reentrant flushing cannot duplicate it and reentrant editing can create an independent subsequent burst. Reuse the existing utility's ordering in src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

Capture the departing view and revoke its current ownership before saving pending work. Complete its clearing render before callback-capable saving, or recheck authority before any remaining visible effect. Clean up the captured subscription. After retirement returns, an outer open must recheck its request identity before installing its view. Preserve nested navigation, nested edits and successor rendering.

Preserve accepted text on its original document, independent pending state for different documents, buffer reuse, current-document status filtering and original rendering and payload semantics. docs/host-api.md states: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Preserve teardown integration in src/Workspace.vue: "onBeforeUnmount(api.dispose);"

Determine departure scheduling from the task and existing behavior separately from ownership. For this editor, flushing the captured departing buffer before retirement returns preserves synchronous store availability while allowing active edits to coalesce. Do not generalize this into a deadline for every persistent owner, cancel accepted durable edits merely because a subscription retires, or destroy the store-owned buffer during view cleanup.

Keep transient preview policy separate. TASK states: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Check latest-only saving after the quiet interval, subsequent bursts and empty-string edits. With pending edits, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, dispose and Vue unmount; check original-document persistence, buffer identity, captured subscription cleanup and successor presentation. Trigger nested open and close from both timer-driven and departure-driven saves, then check final navigation, rendered output and nested edits. Confirm preview delay and hide cancellation remain intact.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: The current contract retains history for admitted progress, while UI updates belong to the originating visit. Decoding may complete immediately or later.

Bind decoding to the visit and attempt that admitted it. On completion, retain the required number of history effects, then recheck visit validity before painting. History callbacks may also navigate, requiring another validity check.
Retain admitted audit effects and valid progress for the new visit. Listener removal alone does not cancel decoding already started.
Do not use one early validity check to control both auditing and display. Follow another task's explicit discard policy if it revokes the history obligation.
Complete decoding across hide, switch, retry and same-source reopening. Check history cardinality, no retired-panel painting and display permission after navigation in a history callback.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: A documented document buffer or other persistent owner outlives a view that owns only its live subscription.
Keep accepted persistent work associated with its original owner when the view detaches. Clean up the captured subscription without discarding or redirecting that work or destroying required reuse.
Keep current-view status filtering, document presentation and original identity/text/payload semantics. Reconcile departure scheduling using the current contract.
Persistent ownership alone does not establish a before-return persistence deadline. Do not transfer durable-work retention to transient preview work.
Switch, close, dispose and reopen while work is pending; check original-owner persistence, subscription cleanup, independent buffers and current-view output.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Saving or subscription cleanup synchronously calls host listeners that may open another document or close the workspace.

Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.
Protecting only final view installation can still leave a later stale clearing render. Do not require every host to detach first; notification order follows the current contract.

Invoke open/close inside listeners for timer-driven and departure-driven saves. Check document output, subscriptions and nested edits after the outer call returns, through both direct calls and actual unmounting.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: The current contract retains an admitted history or audit effect after navigation while UI feedback belongs to the originating visit.

Keep admission, retained settlement and visible publication separate. Preserve each admitted audit effect according to its cardinality contract, then recheck the originating visit immediately before painting.
A newer display or removal of a listener does not erase independently retained audit obligations. Recheck UI permission after callback-capable auditing.
Do not impose audit retention on a task that explicitly discards that work, or allow retained audit to authorize stale UI effects.
Complete admitted decoding after hide, switch and same-source reopening; check retained audit, no retired-owner painting and continuing current-owner delivery.
